title: Cepheus: Accelerating Datacenter Applications with High-Performance RoCE-Capable Multicast
problem: Existing multicast approaches fail to efficiently collaborate with commodity RDMA transport, either causing inefficient multicast traffic transmission or being constrained by insufficient end-host transport protocol capabilities.
motivation: RDMA is becoming the de-facto networking architecture for datacenter applications requiring stringent performance, but combining multicast communication patterns with RDMA remains challenging.
method: Cepheus enables multicast (sending data to many destinations) over RoCE (Remote Direct Memory Access over Converged Ethernet, a protocol for ultra-fast data transfer between computer memories) by putting a translator inside the network switch. Multicast and RoCE fundamentally work differently—they structure data and process it in incompatible ways—so the switch translates between them in real-time. This translation runs on custom hardware (an FPGA) built into the Ethernet switch, allowing the switch to actively assist rather than just passively pass packets through.
key_novelty: The key idea is using hardware assistance inside the network switch to make multicast and RoCE work together, rather than trying to fix the incompatibility at the endpoints.
contributions: RoCE-capable multicast system combining multicast traffic reduction with RDMA performance benefits
In-network switch-based assistance to handle multicast-RDMA incompatibilities
FPGA prototype implementation demonstrating interoperability with commodity RoCE protocol
5.2× faster multicast communication and 2.7× higher replication throughput vs existing RDMA multicast schemes
